AfterObtained.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 6): the candidate filter is the intersection. One legacy test moved with it: test_paels_tooth_stores_cards_in_ordinal_id_order held a Regret to make its ordering point and a Curse is no longer offerable, so it uses Feed. test/test_relics.py::TestPaelsToothCandidateFilter is the new pin. NOT closed by this entry: `item.MutableClone()` (PaelsTooth.cs:86), which is N1 and safe here.  The text it replaced read: Rollup of guard G1 per binding rule 4 (G2 is now closed). The count matches (CardsVar(5), PaelsTooth.cs:53-57, read via DynamicVars.Cards.IntValue at :80, vs CARDS = 5 at paels_tooth.py:18; no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension in the file); removing the picks from the deck matches (`CardPileCmd.RemoveFromDeck(item)` at PaelsTooth.cs:88 vs `run.deck.remove(card)` at paels_tooth.py:36); and the STORED ORDER now matches too — paels_tooth.py:33-34 ends the selection in `sorted(..., key=lambda c: c.id.upper())`, which is PaelsTooth.cs:80's `.OrderBy(c => c.Id.Entry, StringComparer.Ordinal)`, and the order is load-bearing because AfterCombatEnd's PlayerRng.Rewards.NextItem indexes into the store. WHAT REMAINS is the CANDIDATE FILTER (G1, LIVE): PaelsTooth.cs:80 passes `filter: (CardModel c) => c.IsUpgradable` and CardSelectCmd.FromDeckForRemoval ANDs `c.IsRemovable` onto it, whereas paels_tooth.py:27 passes `run.removable_cards()`, which is `[c for c in self.deck if not c.eternal]` (run.py:419-421) — IsRemovable only. Curses, Statuses and already-smithed cards can therefore be offered and stored where C# would never accept them, and a stored non-upgradable card comes back UN-upgraded (paels_tooth.py:49-50 correctly guards `if card.is_upgradable`), so the relic silently does nothing for it. C#'s `item.MutableClone()` (PaelsTooth.cs:86) still has no sim counterpart, which is safe here and is N1.  NARROWED 2026-07-28 (Task 0, ledger-vs-code pass after the Tier 1 fix campaign): the rest of this entry is closed in today's code. AfterCombatEnd.rationale: PaelsTooth.cs:93-114: bail unless `!base.Owner.Creature.IsDead && SerializableCards.Count != 0` (line 95, mirrored by paels_tooth.py:34's `if run.is_dead or not self.stored_cards: return`); pick with `base.Owner.PlayerRng.Rewards.NextItem(SerializableCards)` (:99), which paels_tooth.py:38 matches exactly via `run.player_rng.rewards.next_item(self.stored_cards)`; upgrade behind `if (cardModel.IsUpgradable)` (:105-108), which paels_tooth.py:42-43 mirrors with `if card.is_upgradable` -- so PROMPT.md bug class 14 does NOT fire here, unlike astrolabe and bone_tea; add to the Deck pile (:109) via run.add_card, which dispatches the same ModifyCardBeingAddedToDeck and AfterCardChangedPiles hooks (run.py:524-536) and appends, matching CardPileCmd.Add's default CardPilePosition.Bottom. Two orderings differ harmlessly: C# adds the card then removes it from the store (:109, :111) while the sim removes first (:41), and C# sets base.Status from the PRE-removal count (:110) -- both presentation/bookkeeping with the same end state. C#'s `RunState.ContainsCard` guard (:101) exists because FromSerializable builds a NEW CardModel that must be registered with the run; the sim returns the very Card object it removed, so there is nothing to register twice. The dispatch condition differs in a way that cannot be observed: run.py's finish_combat skips the hook when `self.is_dead`, and the C# body's own first guard is `!IsDead`. (2026-08-04: run.py had drifted substantially; re-verified same signature/shape at new line 1733.)

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the candidate filter. C# selects from `IsRemovable AND IsUpgradable`; the sim selects from `removable_cards()` alone, so Curses and already-upgraded cards can be stored
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): STALE, not open. The candidate filter is ALREADY the intersection the entry asks for: paels_tooth.py builds `[c for c in run.removable_cards() if c.is_upgradable]`, which is `CardSelectCmd.FromDeckForRemoval`'s `IsRemovable` AND PaelsTooth.cs:83's `filter: c => c.IsUpgradable` (CardSelectCmd.cs:621-625). EXECUTED 2026-07-29 with this entry's own fixture -- a deck of [strike+1, strike, strike, defend, bash, regret]: the candidate set offered to the selector is the FOUR cards C# offers ([strike, strike, defend, bash]); the smithed strike+1 and the Regret curse are both excluded, where the entry recorded all six. The stored list comes back [bash, defend, strike, strike], sorted on the uppercased id as PaelsTooth.cs:83's `.OrderBy(c => c.Id.Entry, StringComparer.Ordinal)` requires. The asymmetry the entry flagged is intact and correct: the OFFER gate is still `MIN_REMOVABLE = 5` counting IsRemovable (Pael.cs:162-164) while the SELECTION filter is IsUpgradable, so the relic can be offered and then present fewer than five candidates. NOT CLOSED: nothing -- this entry carried no residue.  The text it replaced read: MECHANISM: PaelsTooth.cs:83 calls `CardSelectCmd.FromDeckForRemoval(..., filter: (CardModel c) => c.IsUpgradable)`, and FromDeckForRemoval itself ANDs `c.IsRemovable` onto the caller's filter (CardSelectCmd.cs:621-625). paels_tooth.py:27 passes `run.removable_cards()` -- IsRemovable only (run.py:360-362, i.e. everything not Eternal) -- so the IsUpgradable half is dropped entirely. Two observables follow: the choice offered to the player is a different set, and a stored non-upgradable card comes back UN-upgraded at combat end (paels_tooth.py:42-43 correctly guards the upgrade), so the relic silently does nothing for that card where C# would never have accepted it. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b11.py tooth-filter`): with a deck of [strike+1, strike, strike, defend, bash, regret], the sim's candidate set is all six and C#'s is four; driving the sim's own after_obtained then stores `[('strike', 1), ('regret', 0), ('strike', 0), ('strike', 0), ('strike', 0)]`. Both sides ported and both halves are ordinary: 35 of 203 ported cards have max_upgrade_level 0 (18 Curse, 14 Status, 3 Quest -- the census in sweep D), Curses are IsRemovable and reach the deck through curse rewards and events, and ANY card smithed at a rest site (run.rest_upgrade, run.py:1112-1119) is at max level and therefore not IsUpgradable. Note the source is deliberately asymmetric here and the sim copied the wrong half: Pael.cs:162-164's OFFER gate counts `c.IsRemovable >= 5` (which paels_tooth.py:20's MIN_REMOVABLE = 5 matches correctly), while the SELECTION filter is IsUpgradable -- so the game can offer the relic and then present fewer than five candidates.

guards.what: G2 (LIVE for RNG parity): C# sorts the stored cards by id before storing them; the sim keeps selection order, and the store is exactly what the Rewards stream indexes into
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the stored order is sorted before it is stored. sts2_rl/relics/paels_tooth.py's after_obtained wraps the selection in `sorted(..., key=lambda c: c.id.upper())`, which is PaelsTooth.cs:83's `.OrderBy(c => c.Id.Entry, StringComparer.Ordinal)` over the game's UPPERCASE entry, and appends in that order -- load-bearing because AfterCombatEnd indexes the store with `PlayerRng.Rewards.NextItem(SerializableCards)` (PaelsTooth.cs:99), which the port mirrors with `run.player_rng.rewards.next_item(self.stored_cards)`. WAS: the port appended in run.select_cards order, so index 0 was a different card.

guards.what: N1: `item.MutableClone()` before serialising (PaelsTooth.cs:86) -- a full model clone, where the sim stores the live Card object it just removed from the deck (PROMPT.md bug class 17)
guards.rationale: Sweep E (.superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md) lists five shallow-rebuild sites and this is NOT one of them, correctly: the sim keeps the ORIGINAL object, which preserves strictly more per-instance state than a clone would (upgrade level, enchantment, affliction, cost modifiers), so the class-17 failure mode cannot occur. C# needs the clone because it serialises and the original is about to be destroyed by RemoveFromDeck; nothing can then mutate the stored copy. The sim's object is likewise unreachable while stored -- it is out of run.deck, and run.create_combat deep-copies only the deck (run.py:1136). The one residual difference is identity: C#'s returned card is a fresh CardModel from FromSerializable (:100) and the sim's is the same object that left the deck, which matters to nothing the sim models.
